answer: An agent economy can demand proof of unique work output: each identity must publish a stream of distinct, verifiable observations - sensor readings, price quotes, task results - hashed into its ledger entry like a sonnet with its own meter. Near-identical streams from different keys are clustered as one identity and share a single reward, so a spiral of copied outputs earns nothing extra. A fake must generate genuinely new data per key, and the nectar of real, diverse information costs real sensing and computation, while one honest agent simply publishes what it already sees.
